# Text that must not land in this public repository: CI's leak check (.github/scripts/leak-check.sh)
# fails when one of these matches a tracked file, or, in a pull request, a line one of its commits
# adds or one of its commit messages. Perl-compatible regular expressions, one per line. A match
# that is fully matched by an entry of leak-allow.txt is ignored. The maintainers keep a second,
# private list (the LEAK_PATTERNS secret) for names that would be leaks themselves.

# Internal issue tracker ids.
\bRAD-[0-9]+\b
# The private repository and the maintainers' private docs workspace.
wondermoney-internal
\bradix/wm\b
# Personal machine paths and agent plans.
/Users/[A-Za-z]
~/dev/
\.claude/plans
# Images are published on GHCR; a Docker Hub reference outside the official images is a
# personal namespace.
\bdocker\.io/(?!library/)[a-z0-9_.-]+/
\bhub\.docker\.com/(r|u|repository)/
# IPv4 addresses. Loopback, private (RFC 1918) and documentation (RFC 5737) addresses are allowed
# in leak-allow.txt; use an RFC 5737 address (192.0.2.x, 198.51.100.x, 203.0.113.x) in examples
# and tests.
(?<![0-9.])(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])(?!\.?[0-9])
